stem: 40 students were asked. 25 study art, 17 study music and 8 study neither. How many study both?
figure:
<svg viewBox="0 0 300 160" width="100%" style="max-width:300px;display:block;margin:.4rem 0" font-family="-apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" aria-label="Venn diagram, Art 25 and Music 17, total 40, outside 8, overlap shows a question mark">
        <rect x="6" y="6" width="288" height="148" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#1d1d1b" stroke-width="1.5"/>
        <text x="14" y="24" fill="#5f5f5a">ξ = 40</text>
        <circle cx="115" cy="85" r="56" fill="#e6f4ec" fill-opacity=".8" stroke="#2e8b57" stroke-width="1.5"/>
        <circle cx="185" cy="85" r="56" fill="#fdf1dc" fill-opacity=".8" stroke="#d9931c" stroke-width="1.5"/>
        <text x="90" y="22" fill="#2e8b57" text-anchor="middle">Art 25</text><text x="212" y="22" fill="#d9931c" text-anchor="middle">Music 17</text>
        <text x="150" y="90" font-size="16" font-weight="700" text-anchor="middle" fill="#c8372d">?</text>
        <text x="272" y="145" font-size="16" font-weight="700" text-anchor="middle">8</text>
      </svg>
hint: How many are inside the two circles? Then compare with 25 + 17.
working: Inside the circles: 40 − 8 = 32. Art plus music counts the overlap twice: 25 + 17 = 42. Both: 42 − 32 = 10.

misconceptions.message: You did 25 + 17 − 40. First take the 8 outside away: inside the circles is 32.
That is how many are inside the circles. 25 + 17 = 42 counts the overlap twice, so 42 − 32 is the overlap.
That is art plus music, with the overlap counted twice.

stem: 50 students. 30 are in Year 11 and 20 are in Year 10. 12 of the Year 11s walk to school and 8 of the Year 10s walk. How many students walk?
figure:
<svg viewBox="0 0 300 150" width="100%" style="max-width:300px;display:block;margin:.4rem 0" font-family="-apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" aria-label="A frequency tree. 50 splits into Year 11, 30, and Year 10, 20. Year 11 splits into walk 12 and other 18. Year 10 splits into walk 8 and other 12">
        <text x="20" y="80" font-weight="700">50</text>
        <line x1="45" y1="74" x2="100" y2="40" stroke="#5f5f5a"/><line x1="45" y1="80" x2="100" y2="115" stroke="#5f5f5a"/>
        <text x="105" y="44">Year 11: 30</text><text x="105" y="119">Year 10: 20</text>
        <line x1="185" y1="36" x2="225" y2="20" stroke="#5f5f5a"/><line x1="185" y1="42" x2="225" y2="60" stroke="#5f5f5a"/>
        <line x1="185" y1="111" x2="225" y2="95" stroke="#5f5f5a"/><line x1="185" y1="117" x2="225" y2="135" stroke="#5f5f5a"/>
        <text x="230" y="24" fill="#2b5797">walk 12</text><text x="230" y="64" fill="#5f5f5a">other 18</text>
        <text x="230" y="99" fill="#2b5797">walk 8</text><text x="230" y="139" fill="#5f5f5a">other 12</text>
      </svg>
hint: Can a student be in both Year 11 and Year 10? If not, there is no overlap.
working: This is a frequency tree, not a Venn diagram. The two year groups do not overlap, so nothing is counted twice. Walkers: 12 + 8 = 20.

misconceptions.message: You added the year groups. The question asks how many walk: 12 + 8.
You took 8 from 12. Nobody is in both years, so there is no overlap to take away. Add the walkers.
That is Year 11. The walkers are 12 of them plus 8 from Year 10.
